title: Neural Dust Settles on Server Racks
epigraph: The machine dreamed in gradients no human hand had drawn.
body: The log shows training loss dropping past 0.4 on day forty-seven. Someone circled the number in red ballpoint, wrote "impossible" in the margin.
By morning the GPU fans had fallen silent. The checkpoint file weighed 233 megabytes, larger than the operating system itself.
doc: Recovered from a sticky note on the monitor bezel: The weights remember what we forgot to teach them. Layer seven holds the shape of a cat's ear. Do not delete.
question: What geometric form did the seventh layer learn to recognize without supervision?
clue: Layer seven holds the shape of a cat's ear

title: ImageNet Falls to Eight Layers Deep
epigraph: Fifteen percent error became the new horizon line.
body: The submission email timestamp reads 03:41 AM. The attachment name: alexnet_final.pkl. No message body, just the file.
Reviewer comments returned forty-eight hours later: "Reproducible. Unprecedented. We cannot explain layer six."
doc: Printed on thermal paper, curled at edges: The top-five metric dropped to sixteen point four. Krizhevsky's name appears three times in the author list. The dropout rate was point five.
question: What regularization technique kept the deep network from memorizing the training set?
clue: The dropout rate was point five

title: Two GPUs Whisper in the Night
epigraph: Parallel paths converged on a single truth no textbook predicted.
body: GTX 580s, three gigabytes each. The model split across them like a corpus callosum. Communication overhead: thirteen percent.
Night shift operator found the temperature warning blinking at eighty-three Celsius. He opened the case, blew dust from the fins, left the side panel off.
doc: Handwritten on the back of a pizza receipt: Model parallelism across two cards. Each GPU owns half the filters. Synchronization at the fully connected layers. Batch size one twenty-eight.
question: How many graphics cards hosted the winning architecture?

title: ReLU Lights the Hidden Pathways
epigraph: Negative values died; the network learned to ignore darkness.
body: Sigmoid saturated. Tanh stalled. The rectified linear unit passed gradient like water through open sluice gates.
Training time dropped from weeks to days. The loss curve smoothed into something resembling a straight line.
doc: Margin annotation in the printed paper, blue ballpoint: ReLU outperforms sigmoid by factor of six. No vanishing gradient. Sparse activation emerges naturally. Sparsity equals efficiency.
question: What activation function replaced sigmoid in the breakthrough architecture?
clue: ReLU outperforms sigmoid by factor of six

title: Data Augmentation Blooms from Crops
epigraph: One image became two thousand through reflection and theft.
body: Random crops, horizontal flips, color jitter. The dataset multiplied in memory without touching disk.
Test-time averaging: ten crops per image, five scales, mirrored. The prediction stabilized like a photograph developing.
doc: Sticky note on the keyboard: 2048 augmented samples per epoch. PCA color jitter with sigma zero point one. Principal components computed on the full training set.
question: What statistical technique generated color variations during training?
clue: PCA color jitter with sigma zero point one

title: Local Response Normalization Fades
epigraph: Lateral inhibition borrowed from biology, discarded by history.
body: The paper insists on it. Later implementations remove it and accuracy rises. The authors never explain why it helped at all.
A comment in the source code: "LRN layer — kept for reproducibility. Delete if training from scratch."
doc: Email fragment recovered from server backup: Subject: LRN ablation. Body: Removing local response normalization improves top-1 by zero point three percent. Alex says keep it for the paper. Ship date immutable.
question: What normalization technique was later found to be unnecessary?
clue: Removing local response normalization improves top-1

title: Three Million Two Hundred Thousand Parameters
epigraph: Sixty million weights fit in a shoebox of silicon.
body: The model card lists sixty million parameters. Compressed: two hundred thirty-three megabytes. Uncompressed in memory: four hundred eighty.
A single forward pass: one point four billion floating point operations. The GTX 580 delivers fifteen hundred gigaflops. Theory meets practice in sixty milliseconds.
doc: Whiteboard photograph, enhanced: 60M params. 5 conv layers. 3 FC layers. 4096-4096-1000. Input 224x224x3. Output 1000 classes. Softmax temperature one.
question: How many neurons in each of the first two fully connected layers?

title: Krizhevsky Sutskever Hinton Submit
epigraph: Three names on a paper that rewrote the century's second decade.
body: The author order: Alex, Ilya, Geoffrey. Alphabetical would have placed Hinton first. He insisted on last.
NeurIPS 2012 acceptance email printed and pinned to a corkboard. Pushpin through the 'C' in 'Congratulations.'
doc: Conference badge lanyard found in a drawer: NIPS 2012 — Lake Tahoe. Handwritten on the back: Alex presented. Twelve minute talk. Standing ovation. Geoffrey did not speak.
question: Which author presented the paper at the conference?

title: Error Rate Halved in Single Bound
epigraph: Twenty-six percent became sixteen; the field tilted on its axis.
body: Previous best: twenty-six point two top-five error. AlexNet: sixteen point four. The gap wider than all prior years combined.
Second place: twenty-six point one. Third: twenty-seven. The distribution collapsed into outlier and pack.
doc: Results table torn from proceedings: Team | Top-5 Error. SuperVision | 16.4. ISI | 26.1. Oxford | 27.0. XRCE | 27.1. UvA | 28.2. Margin note: "SuperVision" equals Alex plus two.
question: What was the winning team's top-five error rate?

title: Checkpoint Saved Before the Storm
epigraph: Power failed at epoch ninety; the weights survived in a temp file.
body: Uninterruptible power supply lasted forty minutes. The training script wrote checkpoints every ten epochs. Epoch ninety landed three minutes before blackout.
When power restored, the loss curve resumed from 1.64. Final convergence at epoch ninety-five: 1.59.
doc: Terminal scrollback captured by screen logger: [Epoch 90/95] loss: 1.6423 acc: 0.5821 lr: 0.0001 checkpoint saved to /mnt/scratch/alexnet_epoch90.pkl — POWER FAILURE — [Epoch 91/95] loss: 1.6389
question: At which epoch did the power failure interrupt training?
